name: Apixaban

discovery.note: Developed from the earlier factor Xa inhibitor razaxaban; co-developed with Pfizer from 2007.

tagline: Twice-daily factor Xa inhibitor and the world's best-selling anticoagulant
summary: Apixaban is an oral anticoagulant that directly and reversibly inhibits factor Xa. It is used to prevent stroke in atrial fibrillation and to prevent and treat venous thromboembolism, and caused less major bleeding than warfarin in the ARISTOTLE trial.
mechanism: Apixaban binds the active site of factor Xa, both free and within the prothrombinase complex, without needing antithrombin. This reduces thrombin generation and therefore fibrin clot formation.
It has no direct effect on platelet aggregation. Its anticoagulant effect can be reversed with andexanet alfa or prothrombin complex concentrate.
uses: Stroke and systemic embolism prevention in non-valvular atrial fibrillation
Treatment of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism and prevention of recurrence
VTE prophylaxis after hip or knee replacement

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: First approved in the EU for VTE prevention after hip or knee replacement.

history.title: ARISTOTLE
history.detail: Apixaban is superior to warfarin for stroke prevention in AF, with less bleeding and lower mortality.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US for stroke prevention in non-valvular atrial fibrillation (December).

history.title: VTE treatment
history.detail: FDA approves use for treatment of DVT and PE after the AMPLIFY trial.

history.title: Reversal agent
history.detail: Andexanet alfa is approved in the US to reverse apixaban and rivaroxaban.

history.title: Generics approved
history.detail: The FDA approves generic apixaban, although US launch is delayed by patent litigation and settlements.

history.title: Medicare negotiation
history.detail: Eliquis is among the first ten drugs selected for US Medicare price negotiation; the negotiated price takes effect in 2026.

safety.boxed_warning: Premature discontinuation increases the risk of thrombotic events; spinal/epidural haematoma may occur with neuraxial anaesthesia or spinal puncture.

facts: Not recommended in patients with prosthetic heart valves or triple-positive antiphospholipid syndrome.
It has relatively low renal clearance among DOACs.

references.title: Granger CB et al. Apixaban versus warfarin in patients with atrial fibrillation (ARISTOTLE). N Engl J Med 2011
